quotes: It is applied in turn with the session's other changes (A13 rule 2): it takes the session's lock only after every change of the session that passed the session check before the sign-out arrived has had its turn, so each of them — admitted before it — completes, its change to the store included, with the pending confirmation and the uploaded file it may need still in place, and leaves nothing in the ended session. A request arriving after the sign-out is refused at the session check.

Its turn comes after every change of the session that passed the session check before the sign-out did, each having taken its place on the lock in that same step (Conventions): each completes, its change to the store included, and leaves nothing in the ended session; a request arriving after it is refused at the session check.

A request that reads or changes an uploaded file first waits for the import lock, and only holding it passes the session check and takes its place on the session's lock: its arrival for the check is when it holds the import lock, so the two locks are always taken import first and no request holds a place on a session's lock while it waits for the import lock (A16 rule 2).
judgement.why: The flow orders and bars requests by physical arrival relative to sign-out, while the State 5 operations delay sign-out's admission until it obtains the import lock and order other changes by which request passes the check first.

witness.initial: Owner session S is valid, and another session holds the instance import lock.
events: The owner sends sign-out for S, which waits for the import lock.
The owner then sends an ordinary project correction in S, which does not need the import lock.
The other session releases the import lock.
outcomes: Physical arrival orders sign-out first, so the later correction is refused with `unauthenticated` (`no_owner_session`).
Sign-out has not passed its check while waiting; the correction is admitted first, commits, and sign-out ends S afterward.
witness.observer: The owner and subsequent project readers observe whether the correction committed.
basis: The owner creates a project in the owner interface, corrects it, or adds a room to it; Cabinet Kernel adds a room for the agent on a project its session is granted (A09 rule 2).

questions: What deterministic order applies to multiple failures of the same kind within one refusal?

quotes: its kinds in the order the operation's Errors list them, one entry for each failing input or record, each naming the field or the identity it concerns.
judgement.why: Ordering repeated encoded failure entries within one refusal is a response-schema and encoding rule owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Whether duplicate Customer v1 values mean repeated mapping entries or repeated values across picked projects
questions: Does a Customer v1 value count as duplicated only when the owner supplies its mapping entry twice, or also when two picked source projects legitimately contain the same v1 customer value?

quotes: The Customer the import makes from a v1 `customer_ref` (R0-80): no v1 value was minted by Registry — in v1 `customer_ref` is an opaque string the caller supplied (L03) — so the import makes one new Customer for each distinct v1 value and links every imported project that named it to that Customer.
judgement.why: The text explicitly makes one Customer per distinct v1 value and links every imported project sharing that value to it, so occurrence in two picked projects is not a duplicate mapping entry.

topics.topic: Whether read-only requests that access an uploaded file acquire the session and import locks
questions: Does a read-only mapping request that reads the session’s uploaded file hold both locks, or are those locks taken only when the request is classified as a change?

quotes: For a change the step runs holding the session's lock — and first the instance's import lock when it reads or changes an uploaded file — and both are released when the step returns, on every path (Conventions, "Locks of an owner request").

A request that reads or changes an uploaded file first waits for the import lock, and only holding it passes the session check and takes its place on the session's lock: its arrival for the check is when it holds the import lock, so the two locks are always taken import first and no request holds a place on a session's lock while it waits for the import lock (A16 rule 2).
judgement.why: The Outputs limit lock-held execution to changes, while the Enforces passage requires every request that reads an uploaded file, including a read-only mapping request, to take both locks.

witness.initial: An owner session has an uploaded file and no migration closure exists.
events: The owner starts a read-only mapping request for the uploaded file.
Concurrently, the owner uploads a replacement file in the same session.
outcomes: Only changes take the locks, so the mapping may read concurrently with replacement and need not observe one serial session state.
Every request reading an uploaded file takes both locks, so mapping and replacement are serial and the mapping describes exactly one upload state.
witness.observer: The owner sees which upload the mapping describes and which confirmation step can be shown.
basis: For each request with picks, names, aliases and Customer values, `capability:owner_sessions.read_uploaded_file` gives the kept file, and `capability:migration_import.read_import_mapping` reads, in `capability:store.read_in_transaction`, what the picks bring in and nothing else (rule 3): their rooms and pointers, each name and alias they arrive under, the Customers it will make, the malformed records (rule 4, an undeclared type among them, A22 rule 7) and every id production holds (rule 5).
Keep an accepted upload in the session's memory, replacing the session's earlier one (A16 rule 2).
